Definitions, metadata gaps & provenance

    Every observation is one supplied-row return at one perturbation level. Episode count and aggregation are unreported. R₀ is the median non-robust return from a documented pure-axis nominal column, fixed from the named reference-axis file; differences between pure-axis nominal vectors are retained. Normalized retention is Z = R / R₀; reliability S(t) = fraction of supplied rows with Z ≥ t. Clipped AUC = mean clip(Z, 0, 1). Low-return fraction uses Z < 0.5; this is not a physical failure or success rate.

    Each pure axis excludes its documented nominal column. Compound level 0 is included because its fixed background is already perturbed. Within each axis, levels have equal weight; summaries give each received axis equal weight. Lowest-20% return averages the six lowest of thirty supplied rows separately at each condition, then averages conditions and axes. This is not the lower tail of a matched cross-axis policy score. Quantiles use linear interpolation. SD uses n − 1.

    The human confirms these are additional evaluations of earlier policies, not extra independent training runs. Keep these axis sets separate; exact row-to-policy mapping for the added files is not supplied. No bootstrap, L1/L2/L3 classification or paired before/after gain is inferred for these new axes. Environment names follow the human ZIP mapping; v5 IDs and MuJoCo follow the supplied notes. Algorithm and TV/KL parameter semantics remain unreported.

    Severity AUC is the trapezoidal return average over the observed shifted magnitude interval, then averaged equally across axes. It differs from reliability AUC, which integrates over return thresholds. Worst-condition mean is the minimum of condition means, not a matched-policy worst-case score. No unobserved severity range is extrapolated.
